name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index 103.8 on 20 Nov, at a 52-week high and 5.0% higher over three months, at the Watch line
state: The DXY dollar index closed near 103.8 on 20 Nov, a fraction below its 52-week high of 103.9 and about 5.0% higher over three months, at the 5% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). Expectations of a December Fed rate rise have supported the dollar while pushing gold to a 13-month low on 16 Nov (Trading Economics). The level is inside the 90–108 range and SOFR stayed within 3bp of the Fed's reserve rate (FRED).
for_you: A stronger dollar raises the cost of dollar-priced imports and of dollar debt for other countries; travellers to the US get less for their currency.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 4.97% has not yet cleared the 4.5% exit line, so Watch holds
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
